observations: Actual full nine-panel sheet viewed before authoring. Panels 2-5 narrow the upper lids and deliberately shift both irises toward screen-right. The screen-left brow is lower with inward downward inclination while the screen-right brow is relatively raised with an opposing tilt. A sealed restrained mouth develops a downturned corner, then gaze and facial tension recover across panels 7-9. Sheet does not show the initial wide-eyed startle, blushing or downcast embarrassment of Caught staring.
left_right_convention: Brow names use screen sides. blink_R closes screen-left and blink_L closes screen-right. Positive aversion_px moves both original iris sprites and iris/sclera shader offsets toward screen-right in source pixels.
approximation: The independent downturned mouth corner cannot be represented by the frozen controls. All mouth channels stay exactly neutral and sealed; no upward sneer, symmetric purse or fake corner depression is introduced. Peak uses 12 source pixels of rightward aversion (5.88 bust pixels), .38/.30 lid closure (13.68/10.8 source-pixel lash travel), -0.65/+0.22 brow translation (6.5 pixels down/2.2 up) and +.50/-.28 tilt (+4/-2.24 degrees). Rigid brows cannot reproduce every drawn contour. Native fidelity and distinctness remain pending.
approval: Accepted reference art does not approve this candidate or animation.
